title: DeepSeek's New Super-Agent Prototype Reduces Coding Task Times to 15.7 Minutes
summary:
DeepSeek's latest autonomous coding framework utilized a two-layer architecture to reduce the 95th percentile of task completion times for synthetic coding work to 15.7 minutes, down from 29.5 minutes for agents using a single session with subagents. The tool, dubbed "Super-Agent," employs a "Router" session to coordinate with human users and a separate fleet of "Worker" sessions to execute complex code fixes in parallel, according to a detailed research essay and a corresponding GitHub repository released by the lab.

The MIT-licensed prototype is designed to identify and resolve bugs independently by monitoring GitHub events and group chats, a move intended to rival Anthropic's Claude Code. While the framework shows promise in internal tests, DeepSeek cautioned that the public release is an exploratory version that differs from its internal system and has not yet been deployed beyond a small, trusted environment. Coinciding with the release, the firm sought to hire more product managers and designers to help refine its agent-based products.

DeepSeek’s Super-agent: A Final Reviewer Explains the Design and Its Limits
Zhihu contributor @tianyi (崔添翼), from DeepSeek’s product department and one of the final reviewers of its Super-agent design article, explains the proposal’s central trade-off: continuity across tasks versus task throughput.
He credits his DeepSeek Harness colleagues, especially lead author Yujia Qiao, with the main write-up, architecture, code and experiments.

"Super" means a layer above the working agent
The name describes an architectural relationship. A Super-agent adds a layer above the main agent doing the work, whereas a sub-agent adds one below it. "Super" is not a claim of superior intelligence.
Cui explicitly rejects the idea that the team has introduced an entirely new theory. In conversations with other teams, he found similar architectures had already been explored months earlier. The harder challenge, he argues, is identifying and committing to the right long-term direction.

The two-layer design responds to an unresolved memory problem
There is still no consensus on how to implement long-term agent memory. As of his post, DeepSeek Harness itself had no built-in long-term memory spanning sessions, though he suggested that might change soon.
Against that backdrop, the team sees maintaining continuity across tasks and sustaining task throughput as a fundamental trade-off in long-running agent systems.
The two-layer architecture offers a way to decompose that problem. Cui does not claim its particular implementation is optimal.

The prototype implements only part of the proposed design
The repository, dsh-superagent-prototype, remains an exploratory prototype.
Some ideas discussed in the article, including decoupling computation from state and execution environments, still require substantial work to implement in DeepSeek Harness. The released code should therefore not be read as a complete implementation of every architectural proposal.

Internal validation leaves substantial deployment questions
Cui attributes the system’s relatively low complexity in internal use partly to deliberate simplifications in engineering and operating scenarios.
The prototype has only been validated in a small, trusted environment inside the company. Broader deployment still faces the open questions identified in Section 8: extending the two-layer architecture, human-agent collaboration beyond sessions, context boundaries and agent-to-agent communication, and security and privacy.
His account presents Super-agent as a direction to investigate, with working internal experience and explicit limits on what has been demonstrated.

selectedTweets.text:
An internal instance running on DeepSeek Harness already exhibits the intended behavior. The same development task continues across group chat and GitHub. The instance also monitors public discussion, identifies the root cause of a reported defect without being mentioned, and opens a fix pull request.
The team published preliminary measurements on synthetic traffic. 

Each round contained roughly three hundred messages, of which about twenty were work requests; the rest were chatter and CI noise. 

Coding work was replaced by a time-consuming tool so that the numbers reflected scheduling rather than code quality. Across five runs the Super-agent completed tasks with a median of 12.4 minutes and a 95th percentile of 15.7 minutes. A single session given a neutral prompt and a subagent tool never delegated and finished at a 95th percentile of 29.5 minutes. 

A single session given an explicit delegation prompt delegated in four of five runs but still showed a longer tail. Removing the direct-delivery subscription path left completion times essentially unchanged while raising Router decisions by about 30 percent and cached tokens from 23.23 million to 31.77 million. 

In a separate Router stress test, raising the arrival rate from one to forty Triggers per minute increased average batch size from 1.0 to 2.8 and per-request duration from 2.5 to 3.9 seconds, while amortized inference time per decision fell from 6.4 to 1.6 seconds.

The same day the essay appeared, the team released dsh-superagent-prototype on GitHub under the MIT license. The repository states that the code is a research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product, that it differs from the internal system, and that some designs in the essay are future directions not present in the published code. The prototype listens to one GitHub repository and, optionally, Feishu. An authorized request opens a Ticket; the work proceeds in its own session and directory; the result returns in the original conversation, often as a pull request. A web panel surfaces items that need a person. The README’s operating principle is explicit: the agent acts only when asked or when a written rule allows it, and it speaks only when someone must act or can use a result.

The essay lists open problems. Sharding the Router would raise throughput but reduce the global continuity the design relies on. Long-running agents will need memory mechanisms that survive context-window limits. Once sessions are no longer the user-facing unit, the mapping between tasks and human attention must be redesigned. Safe collaboration across organizational boundaries and across separate Super-agent instances remains unsolved. Security is called out directly: a compromised cloud loop could reach every attached machine, and credentials must be kept out of model context.

The original Chinese essay is at https://t.co/4ntPusl5tT. A full English translation is at https://t.co/8xXpHWi18V. The research prototype is at https://t.co/MtC5WRiVWc. DeepSeek Harness itself is documented at https://t.co/8rBU6OK7AX. 

The measurements and internal examples come from the design essay; the prototype README states that it does not implement every element described there.
